entry.title: Stephanie Tranquille v New Beginnings Network [2026] FWC 4113
entry.content:
This was an application by New Beginnings Network to vary an unfair dismissal compensation order so that it could pay $5,025 by instalments of $50 per week, citing financial hardship. The Fair Work Commission refused the amount sought but varied the order to allow 10 weekly instalments of $502.50, with superannuation payable on the original due date.

Key holding: Under s 393 of the Fair Work Act 2009 (Cth), the Commission has a broad discretion to permit unfair dismissal compensation to be paid by instalments, exercised by weighing the respondent’s business needs and likely compliance against the applicant’s need to access compensation within a reasonable period.

In McCarron, James v Commercial Facilities Management Pty Ltd T/A CFM Air Conditioning Pty Ltd [2013] FWC 3577 in ordering that compensation be paid in instalments Bissett C said that when considering the time period for the instalment payments to be made the business needs of the Respondent must be weighed against the needs of the Applicant to access the compensation.

entry.title: VBCW and Commissioner of Taxation (Practice and procedure) [2026] ARTA 2312
entry.content:
This was an interlocutory tax review proceeding in the Administrative Review Tribunal. The Applicant sought to amend his Statement of Facts, Issues and Contentions and to expand his grounds of objection concerning trust distributions, Division 40 deductions, balancing adjustment events, and management fees allegedly deductible under s 8-1 of the ITAA 1997. The Tribunal granted leave to amend and exercised the para 14ZZK(a) TAA discretion to allow the expanded objection grounds.

Key holding: The Tribunal has a discretion under para 14ZZK(a) of the Taxation Administration Act 1953 (Cth) to allow a taxpayer to expand the grounds of objection beyond those originally stated.

The Tribunal exercises its discretion in paragraph 14ZZK(a) of the Taxation Administration Act 1953 (Cth) to allow the Applicant to expand his grounds of objection to cover the matters set out at paragraph 95-97 of the Applicant's Statement of Facts, Issues and Contentions.

entry.title: Carbery v Fire Rescue Victoria [2026] FCA 1488
entry.content:
The Federal Court determined a separate question in three related proceedings concerning the fringe benefits tax treatment of contributions reimbursed by Fire Rescue Victoria to firefighters who are members of an income protection scheme. Justice McElwaine held that the apportionment methodology adopted by FRV was reasonable and fair, and answered that the taxable value of member contributions for the period 1 January 2023 to 1 October 2025 was 28.4% inclusive of GST.
